title: Japan's Amazake Becoming Popular as a Health Drink
paragraphs: Amazake, a traditional Japanese drink made from fermented rice, is enjoying a surge in popularity, as people increasingly drink it throughout the year and promote it as a healthy beverage.

There are two main types of amazake. One is made with koji, a type of mold used in Japanese cooking, and the other is made from sake lees, the solids left over after making sake. Koji-based amazake contains no alcohol, so it can be enjoyed by children as well as adults.

Traditionally, amazake was considered a warming drink for winter. Nowadays, however, many people drink it chilled in summer, partly to help prevent summer fatigue. Interest in the drink grew again in the 2010s, when koji became popular as a fermented seasoning. According to the market research company Intage, sales of amazake peak in both winter and summer, and they reached 14.7 billion yen in 2025.

Some local governments are also promoting the drink. In Kumagaya, a city in Saitama Prefecture known for its extreme summer heat, a vending machine selling koji-based amazake was installed at a health center in June. The city believes the drink helps prevent heatstroke. The machine even displays an "amazake index," which uses weather data to recommend when to drink it.

Businesses are also finding creative ways to sell amazake. In the Nagoya area, an advertising company developed a product based on a local legend from the Edo period, while a website called Amazake Hakko Press shares information from about 70 manufacturers across Japan.

The drink is also starting to attract attention overseas. Ferment Base, a company founded at Utsunomiya University, began exporting amazake to the United States in January. Its products, which come in flavors such as black sesame and ginger, are sold at supermarkets in Silicon Valley. The company's president, Mitsuyuki Hiramatsu, said the company believes amazake will be well received in the US because it is considered a healthy drink.
Hiroshi Fujii, who calls himself an "amazake researcher" and has tasted around 600 varieties, said that amazake has now become a staple beverage.
